law.verification: FY 2025-26 / AY 2026-27 under the Income-tax Act, 1961. Thresholds cross-checked on 18 September 2026 against the Finance Act 2023 (ss. 15-17), the Finance (No. 2) Act 2024 and the Finance Act 2025 (no amendment to ss. 44AB, 44AD or 44ADA), and the Income Tax Department e-filing portal. CA sign-off: pending.

testsEvaluated.threshold: Not exceeding 5% of all amounts received
testsEvaluated.finding: Cash of ₹1,00,000 does not exceed 5% of all amounts received (₹90,00,000).

testsEvaluated.threshold: Not exceeding 5% of all payments made
testsEvaluated.finding: Cash of ₹90,000 does not exceed 5% of all payments made (₹86,00,000).
Turnover of ₹90,00,000 does not exceed ₹1 crore, so neither limit is crossed.
No s. 44AE, 44BB or 44BBB income is declared lower than the deemed amount.
The assessee and the business meet the s. 44AD eligibility conditions.
Turnover of ₹90,00,000 is within the s. 44AD ceiling.
AY 2026-27 is not within a s. 44AD(4) bar.

Income was declared under s. 44AD in an earlier year. Declaring ₹2,00,000 now, below even the lowest possible deemed income, ₹5,40,000 (6% of turnover), attracts s. 44AD(4). Total income exceeds the basic exemption.
Declared profit does not meet the s. 44AD deemed income, so income cannot be declared under s. 44AD(1).

groundsForAudit: s. 44AB(e) with s. 44AD(4) — Income was declared under s. 44AD in an earlier year. Declaring ₹2,00,000 now, below even the lowest possible deemed income, ₹5,40,000 (6% of turnover), attracts s. 44AD(4). Total income exceeds the basic exemption.
notes: Section 44AA: The obligation to maintain books of account under s. 44AA is separate from audit and is not evaluated here.

result.reason: Audit is required under s. 44AB(e) with s. 44AD(4).
result.formReason: The accounts are not audited under any other law, so the report is furnished in Form 3CB + Form 3CD.
